title: Divide and Denoise: Empowering Simple Models for Robust Semi-Supervised Node Classification against Label Noise

problem.claim: Semi-supervised node classification with GNNs and pseudo labeling is vulnerable when training labels and pseudo labels are noisy.

gap.claim: Most existing methods assume noise-free training node labels and do not adequately address label-noise effects in message passing and pseudo labeling.

contributions.claim: A label-noise-robust GNN discards the coupled message-passing scheme.
A reliable graph pseudo-labeling algorithm leverages unlabeled-node knowledge while mitigating noisy pseudo-label effects.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper presents a novel reliable graph pseudo-labeling algorithm and describes its denoising designs as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The proposed learning backbone is reported to prevent overfitting to noisy labels and avoid noise propagation.
The proposed designs are reported to achieve exceptional effectiveness and efficiency.
Experiments on benchmark datasets with different levels of label noise are reported to show new state-of-the-art performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Message-passing GNNs and pseudo labeling perform well for semi-supervised node classification.
Noise-free-label assumptions fail in practice, and noisy labels or pseudo labels can cause overfitting, noise propagation, and reduced reliability.
The paper addresses denoising through changes to the model architecture and pseudo-labeling algorithm.
The proposed designs are reported to improve effectiveness and efficiency, with benchmark experiments reporting new state-of-the-art performance.

source_observation.claim: Coupled message passing can propagate the effects of mislabeled nodes through the graph.

interpretation.claim: Separating or simplifying architectural information flow may reduce amplification of label noise.

application.claim: When designing graph models for noisy supervision, evaluate whether message passing couples local errors to downstream nodes.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that discarding coupled message passing is appropriate for all graph tasks or noise patterns.

source_observation.claim: Noisy pseudo labels can undermine model reliability without special treatment.

interpretation.claim: Pseudo-labeling under label noise requires mechanisms that distinguish useful unlabeled-node information from unreliable pseudo labels.

application.claim: Treat pseudo-label reliability as a separate design concern in semi-supervised learning with noisy supervision.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the reliability criteria, error guarantees, or conditions under which the pseudo-labeling algorithm succeeds.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the architecture, algorithm details, datasets, baselines, noise models, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not report computational-cost measurements or independent verification of the claimed performance.
